explanation: Matches the Hilbert–Smith conjecture as stated on Wikipedia (Hilbert–Smith conjecture): a locally compact group acting faithfully and continuously on a connected manifold is a Lie group. X is a connected Hausdorff space charted on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), G a locally compact topological group with a continuous faithful action, and AdmitsLieGroupStructure G (a continuous group isomorphism, i.e. a homeomorphic isomorphism, onto a finite-dimensional real-analytic Lie group, not required second countable) is the conclusion. Not requiring second countability of the Lie group is needed, as the file notes, since uncountable discrete groups act faithfully on connected manifolds. X is not assumed second countable either, but this does not change the problem: it reduces to the ℤ_p case (Wikipedia), and a faithful ℤ_p action on any connected manifold restricts to a faithful action of an open finite-index subgroup (≅ ℤ_p) on a component of a σ-compact invariant open set, which is an ordinary second-countable connected manifold. Note: Wikipedia now reports (October 2026) a claimed proof in all dimensions and a Lean proof registered on Palomar, so the 'research open' tag may need revisiting, but that does not affect the statement's correctness.
